topic: how Brownie Wise made Tupperware a home-party business and was then fired
storyAngle: The woman who made Tupperware a party was fired from it.
doNotClaim: Do NOT say Wise invented the home party; she brought the party plan from Stanley Home Products.
Do not say who fired her (sources split between Tupper and the board) and do not state an ownership stake or a dollar settlement; say only "reportedly about a year's salary".
Do not give reasons for the firing; accounts conflict.

facts.claim: Brownie Wise had sold Stanley Home Products through home parties before she joined Tupperware; she met Earl Tupper in 1951 and became his vice president and general manager.
Wise urged Tupper to pull Tupperware out of retail stores and sell it only through home parties.
She sued and reportedly settled for about a year's salary.
facts.note: sources conflict on amount; do not state a dollar figure
